To answer this question, we need to consider historical trends in food prices and wages in Britain since 1950. Over the decades, due to advances in agriculture, food production, global trade, and supermarket competition, the real cost of food (as a proportion of average wages) has generally decreased. This means that people spend a smaller percentage of their income on food and drink today compared to 1950. Therefore, food and drink have become more affordable over time.
